topic: Everyday brain illusions: stopped clock, blind spot, doorway effect, phantom vibration, frequency illusion
hook: 5 ways your brain lies to you daily
caption:
Your brain doesn't show you reality. It shows you its best guess. Right now there is a hole in your vision, and you can't see it, because your brain fills it in.

These five glitches happen to almost everyone, every day. Researchers have studied each of them, from the 'stopped clock' illusion to phantom phone buzzes.

Which one happens to you the most? 👇

Cover: 5 ways your brain lies to you daily
📷 unknown (CC BY 4.0) via wikimedia

1/5 The frozen clock (1 sec)
Glance at a clock and the first second feels longer. Your brain fills in the gap from your eye movement.
📷 ECTran71 (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

2/5 Your hidden blind spot
Each eye has a spot with no light sensors, where the optic nerve exits. Your brain quietly paints over it.
📷 Osmo Lundell (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

3/5 The doorway effect
Walking through a door can make you forget why you came. Studies suggest your brain files it as a new scene.
📷 A.-K. D. (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

4/5 Phantom vibrations (89%)
In one study, 89% of students felt their phone buzz when it hadn't. Your brain is primed to expect it.
📷 Santeri Viinamäki (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

5/5 Suddenly everywhere
Learn a new word and you see it all the time. It was always there. Your brain just started noticing.
📷 Tomomarusan (CC BY 2.5) via wikimedia
